test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 10th December 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Abhay sold 70% of his goods at a profit of 25%, 40% of the remaining goods at a loss of 40%, and the remaining goods at the cost price. What was his profit/loss percentage in the entire transaction?
solution:
Given:

Abhay sold 70% of his goods at a profit of 25%, 40% of the remaining goods at a loss of 40%, and the remaining goods at the cost price.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let there be 100 items and each cost Rs. 100.

Total cost price = 100 × 100 = Rs. 10000

Selling of the goods sold at a 70% profit = (100 × 70%) × (100 + 100 × 25%)

⇒ 70 × 125 = Rs. 8750

Selling of the goods sold at a 40% loss = ((100 - 70) × 40%) × (100 - 100 × 40%)

⇒ 12 × 60 = Rs. 720

Selling of the goods sold at the cost price = (100 - 70 - 12) × 100 

⇒ Rs. 1800

Total selling price = 8750 + 720 + 1800 = Rs. 11270

Now, the profit percentage = {{11270 - 10000} over 10000} × 100\%

⇒ 12.7%

**∴ His profit percentage in the entire transaction was 12.7%.**
